title: Dedicated capacity: load synchronizer and SLA safeguard playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: build a deterministic, tenant-aware load measurement harness ("Load Synchronizer") and a customer-facing acceptance playbook that proves Dedicated capacity throughput & SLA guarantees. Deliverables: 1) load-synchronizer (orchestrator and config library) that composes realistic multi-tenant request patterns, KV warming, and cache-aware probes; 2) benchmarking methodology and test matrix covering steady, burst, and long-tail profiles; 3) customer acceptance checklist, scripts and dashboards for signoff; 4) automated report generator for SLAs and headroom calculations.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Load Synchronizer can run three canonical scenarios (steady, burst, long-tail) against a dedicated pool and produce repeatable metrics (avg tokens/s, p95/p99 latency, error rate, saturation point). 2) For each scenario, the harness produces a signed report and dashboard link. 3) Onboarding playbook lets a customer run the acceptance suite with <2 hours of RedTeam assistance. 4) If autoscaler triggers in acceptance runs, the policy decision tree logs the event and shows expected recovery time. 5) All tests pass on an internal staging fleet and a pilot customer run yields metric delta <=10% vs internal baseline.
testing_plan: We will implement the harness as a small Go/TS orchestrator + Python metrics collector. Tests are executed from a control VM in the target region to avoid cross-region noise. Steps: (a) configure tenant mix and request tempo file; (b) pre-warm KV cache using 'warm-kv' mode; (c) run scenario, collecting per-token latency, queue depth, GPU utilization, and autoscaler events; (d) post-process into deterministic throughput fingerprint and headroom curve. Each run should include a seeded RNG so runs are reproducible.
test_matrix: Scenario A - Steady: 60m run, 5 concurrent tenants, target per-tenant QPS to hold 70% cluster utilization
Scenario B - Burst: 10m bursts every 30m, 50% of tenants spike x4 concurrently, measure autoscaler reaction and tail-latency impact
Scenario C - Long-tail: 4h run with heavy tail clients (~20% of requests have +2x sequence length), validate KV cache effectiveness
Scenario D - Failure injection: simulate 1 failed replica and a rolling restart during steady-state to validate graceful degradation
Scenario E - Tenant-mix sweep: sweep small->large tenant ratios to find worst-case shared-QoS contours
expected_outputs: JSON report with keys: tokens_per_sec, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, error_rate, autoscaler_events
HTML summary with headroom curve and shaded region for error budget consumption
Dashboard link (Observability) annotated with run ID and PR that kicked off the test
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Autoscaler oscillation during synthetic bursts could mask real headroom. Mitigation: include rate-limited burst profile and observe multiple consecutive bursts before trusting autoscaler behaviour.
Risk: KV warmers overfit to synthetic requests. Mitigation: include replay of sampled production prefixes for at least 10% of runs.
Risk: Customer environment network noise. Mitigation: provide remote support agent and baseline network test to normalize results.
Risk: False confidence from short runs. Mitigation: require at least one long-duration (>=60m) verification run for signoff.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal alpha runs on staging fleet (owners: Ravi, Mei) - 1 week. 2) Iterate on scenarios with Performance and Runtime teams - 2 weeks. 3) Pilot with 2 willing customers (one PLG startup, one mid-market) - 2 weeks support window. 4) Publish playbook and automation in Console as 'Dedicated acceptance kit' and link from onboarding flow.
customer_onboarding_checklist: Schedule 2-hour alignment call and ensure customer provided model version and expected peak QPS
Provision a dedicated pool in the customer's region and share run credentials
Run baseline network and KV warm tests
Execute canonical steady and burst scenarios with RedTeam on call
Review report, confirm SLA headroom, and capture signoff in ticket
